newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says reported telecoms bill an "old draft".
newsitem.headline: Brazil says reported telecoms bill an "old draft".

text.p: A draft of a new telecommunications law, which was widely reported and moved stock prices Tuesday, is not the bill that will be sent to Congress, a spokesman for the Communications Ministry said.
"That was an old version that has undergone several alterations," Francisco Mendonca, the ministry's chief spokesman, told Reuters. "It was not authorized by us."
He declined to say what items had been changed in the bill, but he said the bill to go before lawmakers contains 246 articles, compared to 139 in the draft published by a local newspaper.
A bill creating the new General Telecommunications Law had been expected to go before Congress's lower house this week, but Mendonca said it may actually happen next week.
"It may be this week. It may be next week. I don't have a date yet," he said.

A local news agency on Tuesday published a bill it said would be sent to Congress outlining the creation of a powerful watchdog that will set Brazil's future telecom policy, grant concessions and establish rates.
The report prompted share prices of federal telecoms giant boost local stock markets.
Mendonca criticized news reports of the draft bill, calling the coverage "a festival of nonsense, a real carnival."
In particular, he slammed reports that said the government's role in naming members to the board running the watchdog means the agency will not be independent.
"That's ridiculous," he said. "It's impossible to create an agency not linked to someone."

He also said the draft reported Tuesday did not outline government plans for the break-up and subsequent privatization of the Telebras system, issues that will be addressed in the bill going to Congress.

He declined to give further details of the telecoms bill, which will not cover cellular, satellite or cable TV services, saying Communications Minister Sergio Motta will call a news conference when it is introduced to Congress.
